title: Token-econ workback and role phasing proposal Q2-Q3 2026
summary: A combined budgeting sheet and hiring phase plan that ties token-level pricing sensitivity to month-by-month headcount decisions for the inference product lines (hosted API + dedicated). Includes three pricing shock scenarios, role-by-role hire phasing, and a quick cost/revenue reconciliation to show runway impact and break-even tokens per dollar targets.
content:
Purpose
- Quick workback to convert token demand forecasts into hiring and spend choices across Q2–Q3 2026. Primary goal: identify minimal headcount commitments that keep latency/cost SLAs under pricing shock scenarios while preserving 6–9 month runway under conservative revenue metrics.

Assumptions (base case)
- Avg tokens per request: 600
- Monthly active paying customers: 750 -> projected growth 6%/mo (base)
- Avg revenue per 1M tokens (list price): $10 (hosted blended)
- Effective unit cost today (including infra, licensing, infra ops): $4 per 1M tokens
- Dedicated bookings committed: $1.2M ARR starting May 2026 (aligned to sales pipeline)
- Hiring lead time: 6 weeks for senior infra roles, 4 weeks for junior staff
- GPU procurement lead time for private customers: 12 weeks (capex)

Headcount phasing (proposal)
- Hiring windows tied to month boundaries so ramp aligns with start of monthly billing cycles. Proposed hires and timing: 
  - May 2026: 1 Sr Serving Engineer (on-call lead), 1 Product Finance Analyst (quota expansion modeling)
  - June 2026: 2 SRE (dedicated capacity reliability), 1 ML Infra Engineer (quantization+fp16 pipeline)
  - July 2026: 1 Sales Engineer (dedicated deals), 1 Customer Success (enterprise onboarding)

Rationales:
- Delay junior hires to Q3 where possible to preserve immediate runway. Senior hires early to reduce operational risk for Dedicated contract handoffs.
- Prioritize ML Infra Engineer to capture model-quantization savings that reduce token-unit cost by target 15% within 60 days of hire.

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (three lenses)
1) Mild compression (Scenario A) - prices down 10% from list, demand +8%
   - Revenue per 1M tokens -> $9.00
   - Unit cost initially $4.00; with ML Infra hire and quant savings -> $3.40
   - Gross margin per 1M tokens -> $5.60
   - Estimated monthly tokens (end of Q3) -> 3,700M -> monthly gross contribution ~ $20,720
2) Medium compression (Scenario B) - prices down 20%, demand +15%
   - Revenue per 1M tokens -> $8.00
   - Unit cost improved to $3.60 after optimizations
   - Gross margin per 1M tokens -> $4.40
   - Estimated monthly tokens -> 4,150M -> monthly gross contribution ~ $18,260
3) Severe compression (Scenario C) - price down 35%, demand +25% (price-led growth)
   - Revenue per 1M tokens -> $6.50
   - Unit cost floor (even with optimizations) -> $3.20
   - Gross margin per 1M tokens -> $3.30
   - Estimated monthly tokens -> 4,600M -> monthly gross contribution ~ $15,180

Quick runway impact (base vs scenarios)
- Baseline monthly cash burn (pre-hires): $1.05M (ops + payroll + run-of-house)
- Incremental monthly burn from proposed hiring ramp: +$210k by July run rate (fully ramped salaries + benefits + recruiting amortization)
- Net monthly cash flow: revenue contribution (from token economics above) minus burn ->
  - Scenario A: +$20.7k - $1.26M => net burn ~ $1.24M (improved vs baseline due to higher token revenue)
  - Scenario B: +$18.3k - $1.26M => net burn ~ $1.24M (slightly lower uplift)
  - Scenario C: +$15.2k - $1.26M => net burn ~ $1.24M (worst margin; pricing change compresses contribution)
Notes: the headline net burn remains close across scenarios because token revenue ramps are multi-month; the value of hiring early is more risk mitigation and enabling contract delivery than immediate net cash improvement.

Break-even tokens per $1 of spend (sensitivity workback)
- With proposed cost structure, break-even tokens per $1 (monthly) where contribution covers incremental burn:
  - If contribution margin per 1M tokens = $4.40 (Scenario B), need ~30M tokens to cover $132k incremental monthly burn (post-hire) -> ~3.0M tokens per $1
  - If contribution margin per 1M tokens = $3.30 (Scenario C), need ~40M tokens -> ~2.5M tokens per $1
(These are quick ballparks for conversation - we should reconcile with subscription/microtransaction revenue mix.)

Capex vs Opex tradeoff notes
- Private deployments require upfront capacity commitment (capex) where reserved GPU pools reduce per-token infra cost by ~18% vs burst public cloud. However, capital outlay pushes cash burn in short term.
- Proposal: for incoming private deals that exceed $350k ARR, elect to do reserved pool financing with 12-month amortization (finance will model lease vs buy). For smaller deals, use cloud-burst model and pass premium to customer.

Open questions / to-dos
- Validate the 15% quantization savings assumption with ML infra: action item JIRA-PL-987 assigned to @Marta to run two representative models through current quant pipeline. Due 2026-04-20.
- Confirm GPU procurement lead times with procurement vendor; possible variant: if we vendor through partner X, lead time can drop to 8 weeks. Contact: procurement@redwood.ai (ticket PROC-112).
- Sales alignment: can Sales Ops commit to bundling a 6-month upfront for a 10% premium on list price for Q3 dedicated deals? If yes, we can front-load revenue and make earlier hires safer.

Recommended next steps (30/60/90)
- 30d: Run the quantization experiment (Marta). Produce conservative and optimistic unit-cost projections.
- 60d: Freeze hiring plan for Sr Serving Engineer + ML Infra Engineer; begin recruiting; secure 12-month amortization financing approval for capex.
- 90d: Re-evaluate token demand projection vs actual bookings; if bookings l/delta < -15% vs forecast, pause non-critical junior hiring and renegotiate reserved pool schedules.

Notes-to-self (voice memo style)
- This sheet intentionally conservative on early revenue; hires are primarily insurance for SLA and enterprise handoff. Still need to capture upside scenarios where price holds and demand accelerates.
- Keep a short one-pager for the board that shows: (A) hiring schedule, (B) worst/best case monthly net cash flow, (C) one-sentence mitigation per risk.

Appendix: quick micro-budgets (monthly incremental)
- Sr Serving Eng comp (fully loaded): $28k/mo
- ML Infra Eng comp (fully loaded): $23k/mo
- 2x SRE (fully loaded): $36k/mo
- Sales Eng + CSM combined: $24k/mo
- Recruiting + hiring overhead amortized: $5k/mo
- Additional infra buffer (reserve for private deals): $16k/mo
Total incremental run-rate by July: $132k/mo (this number used above)

References and links
- Confluence: Token Economics Working Notes (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: PL-987 (quant pipeline experiments); FIN-210 (capex amortization schedule)
- Slack: #finance-inference (thread: dedicated-capex-ask, pinned messages)

Status / approvals needed
- Finance Ops approval to proceed with 2 hires in May and June (Aisha, sign-off)
- Procurement confirmation on vendor options by 2026-04-30
- Sales commitment on bundling early payment incentives (Sales Ops)

End.
